## What is in this repository

```
outputs/structure/   the extraction prompt, Trimen's structured record, three audit examples, the structuring runbook
outputs/identity/    the merge rules and loop, the approach document, a sample of twelve clusters, the first 25 ledger entries
outputs/ground/      place-grounding cache rows for Victoria, South Africa, Penang, Perth; Brewster's record
outputs/ground-test/ twenty entries for the grounding test, the answer key with MCP lookups, the Gemini run and its scoring
outputs/audit/       the structuring error catalogue, the every-tenth reviewed pairs, the September 2026 project review, the running fixes list
outputs/atlas/       kg_stats for both corpora, the atlas meta.json, the Wodehouse bridge records, the essay on grounding
annotate/            the mark-up exercise (static HTML + bios.json)
review/              the decision exercise (static HTML + cases.json)
source-pack/         Trimen's seven Colonial Office List entries
archive/tropical/    the earlier draft built on The Tropical Agriculturist, kept for reference
```

## The dataset

Everything here is drawn from [Imperial Careers](https://github.com/jburnford/col_matching) (data CC0, code MIT, [DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21079938](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21079938)). The finished graph is committed there as JSONL under `data/kg/graph_stage3/` and `data/iol/graph_stage3/`; the README shows how to load it into LadybugDB or Neo4j in two commands. The pipeline code, the grounding caches and the method documents are in the same repository.

## Rebuilding the exercise

```bash
python3 scripts/build_review_cases.py      # cases.json for the decision exercise
python3 scripts/demo_ditto_fix.py          # before/after records and bounded checks
```

No network needed.

## Running the grounding test

`outputs/ground-test/bios.md` has the twenty entries. For the chatbot column, paste them into any model without tools. For the retrieval column, use the [WikidataMCP](https://wd-mcp.wmcloud.org/) server (Streamable HTTP endpoint `https://wd-mcp.wmcloud.org/mcp`) from a coding agent, or its public search endpoint. Two things to know:

- **Use the vector search, not the string search.** Wikidata's ordinary search API matches labels by string similarity. The MCP server's `search_items` uses semantic embeddings. It is rate limited; cache what you retrieve.
- **No identifiers from memory.** Tell the agent, and check its output. Resolve every identifier you are given before you keep it; `wbgetentities` with a list of ids is enough to see what they are.

## Running the structuring prompt

`outputs/structure/extraction-prompt.txt` is the system prompt. Send it with one entry as the user message to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint and ask for JSON. The Imperial Careers repository's `col_match/kg/extract.py` is the production version, with the validator that drops any place or year not present in the source.

The endpoint can be a hosted service such as OpenRouter (an API key, pay per token), a model you serve yourself with vLLM on a desktop GPU, or a batch job on a research cluster. The [glossary](glossary.qmd#three-ways-to-run-it) compares the three as the project used them, with a worked cost estimate.

## Credentials

No file in this repository contains a credential, and none is needed for the exercises. If you configure an agent with an API key, keep it out of the repository.
